Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 4-6) demonstrate massive tracheobronchomegaly with marked dilation of the trachea and main bronchi, along with extensive cystic bronchiectasis and large cavities containing air-fluid levels that communicate with the dilated airways. These findings are pathognomonic for Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly), distinguishing it from other causes of bronchiectasis or cavitary disease.
